title: Best practices for structuring controller files in Express?
content: Hello everyone! When building a larger REST application, is it preferred to keep business logic in separate service files or inside the controllers? Looking for recommendations on maintaining testability.

replies.content: Great question, Alex! In enterprise apps, separating routes -> controllers (handling req/res) -> service layer (business logic & rules) -> data store makes unit testing much cleaner without needing to mock Express objects.
Thank you Professor! That makes total sense. I will modularize the assignment controller accordingly.

title: JWT Secret and Token Expiration strategies
content: What is the recommended token refresh strategy for single-page applications to ensure users are not abruptly logged out during prolonged sessions?

replies.content: We typically pair short-lived access tokens (15-60m) with rotating refresh tokens stored in secure, HttpOnly cookies. We will cover this in Module 4!

title: Wireshark filters for detecting ARP poisoning and MITM attacks
content: What are the most effective display filters in Wireshark to quickly isolate duplicate IP assignments and gratuitous ARP floods in a local switched subnet?

replies.content: Use rp.duplicate-address-frame and rp.opcode == 2 to spot reply floods. Also keep an eye on MAC address changes for default gateway entries.

title: LoRA vs QLoRA: Memory reduction trade-offs during fine-tuning
content: When fine-tuning on a 16GB VRAM GPU, does 4-bit quantization in QLoRA significantly degrade token output quality compared to standard 16-bit LoRA?

replies.content: In empirical benchmarks (like the QLoRA paper by Dettmers et al.), NF4 (NormalFloat4) achieves nearly identical perplexity to 16-bit LoRA while cutting memory usage by over 60%. Highly recommended for single-GPU setups!
